```dafny
/**
 * Converts a sequence to a freshly allocated array.
 * 
 * Specification:
 * - Input: A sequence `xs` of type `T`
 * - Output: An array `a` of type `T[]`
 * 
 * Postconditions:
 * 1. Fresh allocation: `a` is a newly allocated array (not aliased to any existing array)
 * 2. Length preservation: `|a| == |xs|` (array length equals sequence length)
 * 3. Content preservation: For all indices i, `a[i] == xs[i]`
 * 4. Type correctness: `a` is an array of type `T[]`
 * 
 * Ghost variables may be used to track ordering and element equivalence.
 */
```

## Dafny Implementation

```dafny
method ToArray<T>(xs: seq<T>) returns (a: array<T>)
  ensures fresh(a)  // Fresh allocation
  ensures a != null  // Valid array
  ensures a.Length == |xs|  // Correct length
  ensures forall i: int :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> a[i] == xs[i]  // Content preservation
  ensures a.Type == T  // Type correctness (implicit in Dafny's type system)
  ensures multiset(a[..]) == multiset(xs)  // Same elements (ghost property)
  ensures a[..] == xs  // Same order and elements (strongest guarantee)
{
  // Allocate fresh array with same length as sequence
  a := new T[|xs|];
  
  // Ghost variable to track progress
  ghost var remaining := xs;
  ghost var idx := 0;
  
  // Copy elements from sequence to array
  while idx < a.Length
    invariant 0 <= idx <= a.Length
    invariant a.Length == |xs|
    invariant forall j: int :: 0 <= j < idx ==> a[j] == xs[j]
    invariant remaining == xs[idx..]
    decreases a.Length - idx
  {
    a[idx] := xs[idx];
    idx := idx + 1;
    remaining := xs[idx..];
  }
  
  // Postcondition verification (ghost assertions)
  ghost {
    // Verify order equivalence
    assert forall i: int :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> a[i] == xs[i];
    
    // Verify array content matches sequence
    assert a[..] == xs;
    
    // Verify fresh allocation (implicit from 'new' operator)
    // Dafny's 'fresh' predicate ensures this
  }
}
```
